extra.message: case_bundle_thaw_171 calls pickle.loads() on raw request body (or a GET 'blob' param, optionally base64-decoded) with no validation. Pickle deserialization of attacker-controlled bytes allows arbitrary code execution. The endpoint is only gated by a static shared-secret header (_wrk_gate), not real authentication, so anyone who obtains/guesses INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can achieve RCE.

case_formula_cast_253 passes the user-supplied 'expr' GET parameter directly to eval(). Although __builtins__ is set to {}, this is a well-known incomplete sandbox (e.g. via ().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__() gadget chains) and still allows arbitrary expression evaluation / code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)

extra.message: case_jinja_cast_385 builds a Jinja2 Template from the string concatenation of a fixed prefix and the user-controlled 'fragment' GET parameter, then renders it. An attacker-supplied fragment such as {{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__ }} enables server-side template injection leading to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Server-Side Template Injection)

extra.message: case_dock_shelf_392 builds a filesystem path by joining BASE_EXPORT_DIR with the raw, unsanitized 'name' GET parameter, then writes the request body to it. A value like ../../../../etc/cron.d/evil or an absolute path lets an attacker write arbitrary files outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR, potentially achieving remote code execution or overwriting critical files.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: case_mongo_lane_414 parses the raw JSON request body and passes the 'filter' object (or the whole payload) directly as the MongoDB query filter to find_one(). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g. {"$where": ...} or {"$ne": null}) to bypass intended filtering logic or extract unintended data.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: case_xml_fold_455 builds an lxml XMLParser with load_dtd=True and resolve_entities=True and feeds it the raw, attacker-controlled request body. This configuration allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks that can read local files or make the server issue outbound network requests (SSRF via external entities).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: case_banner_fold_016 concatenates the user-supplied 'copyline' GET parameter directly into an HTML response without any escaping, then returns it as text/html. An attacker can inject <script> or other markup for reflected cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: case_origin_mirror_374 reflects the client-supplied Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This combination lets any origin make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: case_wire_tally_212 logs the full raw request body and the Authorization header verbatim at WARNING level. Bearer tokens, API keys, or other secrets sent by callers are persisted in plaintext application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: case_trust_drift_434 creates an unverified SSL context (ssl._create_unverified_context()) and uses it for an outbound HTTPS request, disabling both certificate validation and hostname verification. This allows man-in-the-middle attacks against the outbound connection.

case_nonce_roll_404 generates a 'code' (named/used as a nonce/token) using Python's random module, which is not cryptographically secure and is predictable/seedable. Security-sensitive tokens or nonces should use secrets.choice/secrets.token_urlsafe instead.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: case_pref_munge_017 merges an attacker-controlled JSON object directly onto a workset dict containing privileged fields like 'is_admin' and 'credit_limit' via workset.update(change_set), with no allow-list of permitted keys. A caller can flip is_admin to true or set an arbitrary credit_limit.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: case_matter_fold_018 returns a hardcoded live-looking partner sync token ('sync_key': 'tok_live_partner_sync') and what appears to be a hardcoded SSN-format value ('tax_ref': '739-44-1982') in every response. Hardcoded secrets embedded in source/response bodies risk credential leakage.

case_identity_hint_364 authenticates callers against a hardcoded dict of short numeric 'verifier' codes ({'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}) compared with a non-constant-time '!=' operator. The codes are hardcoded secrets embedded in source, are only 4 digits (brute-forceable), and the comparison is vulnerable to timing side-channel analysis.

case_pulse_spill_346 raises a RuntimeError that embeds the internal server path BASE_EXPORT_DIR and returns str(exc) directly in the JSON error response. This discloses internal filesystem layout to any caller.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: case_trace_panel_444 returns the DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment variable and the internal BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path in a JSON response, disclosing internal server configuration and layout details to any caller with the shared ops token.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: case_frame_slip_424 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and Content-Security-Policy to an empty string on its response, disabling browser-side XSS mitigations for that response.

_wrk_gate, which guards every 'ops' endpoint in this file, compares the caller-supplied 'x-internal-token' header to the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN secret using Python's '==' operator instead of a constant-time comparison (e.g. hmac.compare_digest). This is vulnerable to timing-based side-channel attacks that can help recover the shared secret, and the shared static-token model itself provides much weaker authentication than per-user auth for the wide range of sensitive operations these endpoints expose.
